commit.message: Suppression Validity aware release
User Delivery Hardening
Update pages.yml
pages and release 0.3.0
v0.3.0: drishti profiles + hardening, README overhaul, CI, landing site

docs: user-facing README — hero banner, 60-second try-it, MCP usage, post-ship priorities

Add assets/smriti-hero.svg (intro banner visualizing bi-temporal supersession);
lead README with install/quickstart/MCP/benchmark-it-yourself from a user's POV;
roadmap reorganized into Shipped + clearly-visible Next priorities (post-ship),
sqlite-vec deferred but prominent. Clean repo: untrack stray :memory: scratch
files and per-build patches (git history is the audit trail), add pyproject
console script. py_compile + 33 tests + HTML/SVG validation all pass.

Build: MCP server (drop-in memory for any MCP agent)

smriti/mcp_server.py — stdlib-only newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdio (no mcp
SDK, zero new deps). 6 typed tools returning structured JSON: remember, recall,
search, facts_about, add_fact, stats. Lite/offline by default; full mode via
env/flags. Security per Codebase-Memory blueprint: SQLite ATTACH/DETACH
authorizer, db path fixed at launch (no traversal), input size caps, malformed
JSON-RPC + tool exceptions caught (loop never crashes). console script
smriti-mcp. +4 tests, 33/33; stdio smoke verified.

README: lead with tested production wins + ship-and-verify (not benchmark deficit)

Reframe positioning around what users actually win — one-line/zero-dep run,
nothing to break, cheap by design, predictable at scale + non-destructive
history, readable/verifiable — each grounded in a tested reality (offline tests,
scale harness, hardening, supersession, measured per-query cost). Replace the
'we haven't benchmarked / competitors challenged' framing with a confident
bring-your-own-benchmark stance.

Build 12 validated: multi-session +10.3 (p=0.046), knowledge-update +1.3 — tax gone

Per-type router delivers the multi-session gain without the knowledge-update
regression. Fill landscape multi-session number (+10 pts, p<0.05); record the
focused A/B in BENCHMARKS.md as the shipped default config.

landscape: add 'why SMRITI for production' top-5 positioning (infra/cost/trust/scale)

Leads with production-fit value props (zero-infra single file; updates-not-deletes
vs delete-on-write rot at 50k; reproducible vs self-graded; cheap+Apache no gated
tiers; per-type routing). Multi-session number left as a marked placeholder to
fill once the final A/B lands.

Build 12: observations are recall-profile only (fix knowledge-update laundering)

Diagnostic (knowledge-update, n=78): full stack 0.756 vs raw 0.808 (-5.1), every
break a stale/superseded value served in place of the current one (mortgage
$350k not $400k, therapist biweekly not weekly, 3 issues not 5). Cause: obs/digest
summaries flatten temporal progressions into authoritative text without
CURRENT/SUPERSEDED markers. Fix: retrieve() include_observations gate; context()
includes observations ONLY on the aggregation path, precision path uses raw
validity-annotated facts (proven 0.808). +test, 29/29.

Build 11: per-type router — isolate recall expansion to aggregation (fix n=300 regression)

Root cause of the n=300 knowledge-update -13: Build 9 key expansion polluted the
shared statement FTS + embedding globally. Fix: keys now live in a SEPARATE
fact_keys_fts index + embeddings stay clean (statement only); the recall profile
(aggregation queries) consults the key channel + semantic-entity linking, while
every other query takes the unchanged precision path. Aggregation gate tightened
(dropped 'how often'/bare 'different' that caught current-state questions).
Agile per-type profiles in context(). +1 test, 29/29.
docs: n=300 A/B report + competitive landscape (HTML)

Build 10: mem0-inspired recall levers (Porter stemmer + semantic entity linking)

Two zero-dependency, off-by-default, A/B-able levers from mem0's 2026 layer:
- stem: FTS5 Porter stemmer so conjugation variants match (keyword normalization)
- semantic_entities: cosine query->entity-name embedding match to reach entities
  lexical token matching misses ('my cousin Rachel' -> 'Rachel'); additive,
  lexical hits stay first. bench: --stem / --semantic-entities; ab_features.sh
  4-arm harness. Tests passing (28).
ab.sh: BASELINE flags applied to both arms (isolate a marginal change)

Build 9: recall track — fact-augmented key expansion (A) + aggregation tally path (B)

Part A (write-time, full mode): extraction emits search_keys (category/synonym
terms, zero extra LLM calls); indexed with the statement in FTS + embedding so
'citrus' finds a 'lime' fact. Clean statement preserved for display.
Part B (read-time, intent-gated): is_aggregation_query() routes counting/total
questions to a high-recall pass (k_agg, wider per-channel) with an enumerate-
and-count instruction that resists abstention. Non-aggregation queries take the
byte-identical existing path (gating test proves no-harm). bench: --key-expansion,
--aggregate. +3 tests, 25/25.
docs: BENCHMARKS.md — n=200 observation-stack A/B (+4.8 overall, per-type, p~0.095)
ab.sh: let QTYPE= clear the type filter (all-types runs)

Build 8: numeric/sum digests + ab.sh SAMPLE support

compute_numeric_totals() sums same-unit quantities (currency, hours, days, …)
deterministically in Python and carries the total into observations/digests, so
SUM-type aggregation questions ('how much total money / hours') get a trustworthy
pre-computed total instead of relying on LLM arithmetic. ab.sh gains SAMPLE for
larger stratified A/B runs. +1 test, 22/22.

harden: network retry + per-question fault tolerance + partial-result flush

_post_json retries transient errors (the socket.timeout that killed a full-S run
at 52/80). run_longmemeval wraps each question in try/except (one flaky question
skips, not aborts) and checkpoints results every 10 questions so a wall-clock
timeout keeps progress. +1 test, 21/21.

docs: update roadmap — mark shipped builds, add post-benchmark next steps

Shipped: observations (+ additive/enumerate/multi-granularity), 2-hop, rerank,
iterative, harness hardening. Next (post-bench): entity canonicalization,
recursive-CTE N-hop, sqlite-vec ANN, incremental refresh, MCP server+security
(borrowings from Codebase-Memory paper), dim guard, namespacing.

Build 7: multi-granularity digests (predicate-level, cross-entity aggregation)

refresh_observations now also emits per-(subject,predicate) digests that
enumerate every object across all entities/sessions (kind='observation',
predicate='digest:<pred>'). Targets the cross-entity totals per-entity
summaries structurally miss (camping trips, distinct doctors, babies, charity
totals) — the MemGAS multi-granularity lesson. +1 test, 20/20.

Build 6: observations additive + enumerate (fix crowding-out & wrong-totals)

Fix 1: observations get their own context slots (obs_k), never displacing raw
facts/episodes from the k budget; rendered as a dedicated ENTITY SUMMARIES
section with a verify-against-facts caveat. Fix 2: observation prompt enumerates
every instance instead of asserting possibly-incomplete totals. Informed by
Mastra Observational Memory (SOTA) + MemGAS multi-granularity. +1 test, 19/19.
run_all.sh: FEATURES env to enable --observations/--iterative on full-mode steps
bench/ab.sh: one-command A/B of a feature flag with accuracy delta
bench: --question-type filter to focus a single gap (e.g. multi-session A/B)

Wire Builds 1/4/5 into the benchmark harness (opt-in flags for A/B)

bench/run.py: --observations (refresh_observations after ingest), --iterative
(context_iterative), --reranker-url/-model/-key (HTTPReranker). Runners gain
observations/iterative params, guarded to full mode. +1 integration test, 18/18.

Build 5: iterative retrieval for multi-hop (full mode, optional)

mem.search_iterative()/context_iterative(): after the first pass, the LLM
proposes a follow-up query for the missing piece (DualRAG-style), a second
retrieval runs, and results merge. Degrades to single-pass without an llm.
+1 test, 17/17 passing.

Build 4: optional cross-encoder reranking (RRF + rerank, Hindsight-style)

New smriti/rerank.py (MockReranker, HTTPReranker for TEI/Jina/Cohere /rerank).
retrieve() materializes a larger fused pool then re-sorts by a model-agnostic
reranker and tags results 'rerank'. Wired through Smriti(reranker=...). Opt-in,
stdlib-only core. +1 test, 16/16 passing.

Build 2: 2-hop entity traversal (graph-lite multi-hop)

Extend the sambandha channel with a bounded, down-weighted second entity hop
so facts one link away from query entities are reachable (Rachel->Acme->Berlin).
Pure SQL over the existing entities table, no graph DB. +1 test, 15/15 passing.
Build 1: observation/summary layer (Hindsight observation paradigm) — +2 tests, 14/14 passing
baseline: original Smriti + benchmark hardening (download, deepseek, sampling, dir-create, UA fix)
